entries.subject:
Primary request: an EARLY CONTINUOUS PAPERMAKING MACHINE inspired by Nicolas Louis Robert's 1798 design and the Science Museum wooden scale model. The core readable sign is a continuous PALE WHITE PAPER WEB on a moving screen through rollers, NOT a pile of individual paper sheets.
Subject: a compact horizontal rectangular light-brown timber frame on four short legs. A shallow, broad, wooden vat with a dark iron hoop sits within the frame under the forming part. Above it, a visibly continuous fine wire-mesh moving screen loops taut around TWO horizontal end rollers, forming a simple coherent flat conveyor path over the vat. Hint at pale grey wet pulp on its back section; keep the mesh as restrained texture, not a busy grid.
At the right/outlet end, a SINGLE pair of large clearly separated wooden pressing rollers with dark iron shafts grips ONE broad bright ivory-white paper strip. The strip emerges between the pressing rollers and curls gently DOWN at the front-right edge, with its clean white surface dominant and its upper end visibly still feeding through the rollers. This is one connected strip, not floating fabric, disconnected paper fragments or toilet-roll spool. Keep the outlet and paper unobstructed.
A small side iron crank with a coherent shaft and modest pair of connected gears is integral to the machine. Use the early wooden-frame and vat vocabulary, but simplify to bold compact masses. No towering drying cylinders, modern stainless factory, giant plant, human museum figure, table, full workshop, steam engine, black backdrop or extra accessories. No letters or printed writing anywhere. Machinery plus its forming paper is ONE functional group.
entries.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, an already-created Victoria 3 technology icon.
Make ONE very small correction only: remove the tiny stray light-colored speck floating in the empty transparent space at the far LOWER LEFT beneath the machine, around x=100, y=1195 on the 1254-pixel square. Also remove any isolated stray pixel flecks in exterior empty space. Restore genuine fully transparent alpha there.
Keep the ENTIRE machine and paper completely unchanged: identical brown wood frame, vat, wire conveyor with pale pulp, twin wooden pressing rollers, continuous plain white paper strip emerging through the rollers, side meshing gears and crank, viewpoint, proportions, lighting, shading, brushed matte material colors, scale and positions. Do not redesign, shift, recolor, add or subtract any part of the machine. Do not change or enlarge the paper. Do not add shadows, words or a backdrop.
Output remains SQUARE, same resolution, genuinely transparent exterior and openings, no checkerboard, no ground, no shadow beneath. This is a tiny background-artifact cleanup, NOT a new composition.
